purpose: Four observations per parent per arm. pre_fix and fix are different frozen versions (proof the fix worked); fix, r2 and r3 are the same frozen version (proof of stability on the fixed version).

parent_selection.catalogue_rule: every fragment in SCOUT_FRAGMENTS attached at every heavy atom of the parent

pre_fix.description: Frozen version before the choose_strategy repeat fix.

fix.description: Frozen version after the fix; first verification run.

r2.description: Second repetition of the fixed frozen version.

r3.description: Third repetition of the fixed frozen version; completes the '≤3 times' target.

observations.what: Decision loop after finding qualifying candidates
observations.evidence: aniline pre_fix terminated as decision_loop with 2 qualifying molecules unfinalised; aniline fix, r2 and r3 all terminated cleanly with no decision_loop.
observations.status: Defect eliminated across three independent post-fix observations.

observations.what: Toluene reaches goal_met on the fixed version
observations.evidence: toluene fix q=1 best=0.01874; r2 q=3 best=0.01874; r3 q=1 best=0.01874. Same best delta (0.01874) and same molecule across three repetitions.
observations.status: Stable on toluene: 3/3 goal_met with identical best delta 0.01874.

observations.what: Phenol variability on the fixed version
observations.evidence: fix q=0; r2 q=1 best=0.01478; r3 q=0. Two of three fixed-version runs did not find a qualifying product.
observations.status: 1/3 goal_met. Phenol needs more than one attempt to reliably reach the 0.01 threshold.

observations.what: Aniline variability on the fixed version
observations.status: 1/3 goal_met. Two of three runs returned early negative results. Aniline has higher variance than toluene.

observations.what: Rule arm never finds qualifying on any parent
observations.evidence: 0 qualifying across 12 rule-arm runs (3 parents x 4 versions).

observations.what: Phenol r3 had its own distinct failure mode
observations.evidence: termination_outcome=execution_failure with reason=consecutive_errors after 19 steps. The model emitted three rejected actions in a row: a select_edit with an unrecorded task-experience ID, a repeated choose_strategy on an already-selected hypothesis (rejected by the new fix), and a choose_strategy that placed the free-text reason inside arguments. Network: 0 failures, 0 retries.
observations.status: Single observation. Not a defect of the fix (the second rejection was correct and the fix did its job); the issue is that the consecutive_errors budget was exhausted before the model could recover from one well-formed rejection. The protocol's error budget of 3 is unchanged and not adjusted here.

observations.evidence: 12 agent-arm runs in this summary, 0 network failures, 0 network retries.

honest_limitations: Three observations per parent on the fixed version is the '≤3' ceiling, not a statistical sample.

Toluene 3/3 vs phenol 1/3 vs aniline 1/3 is real but explained: toluene has 6 reachable qualifying products in the catalogue, aniline 2, phenol 3, so toluene has more headroom for the agent to hit the threshold.
The parent-derived catalogue is larger than the original phenol catalogue, so cross-version comparison is about mechanism, not effect size.
Rule arm found 0/12; it is a weak baseline and cannot be used to claim the agent is better.
No docking, no biological validation, and the 0.01 threshold is unchanged.
